steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A hypothesis is a testable statement that predicts the outcome of an investigation.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A good hypothesis is specific, measurable and can be tested using data.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The null hypothesis (H₀) states there is no difference, no effect or no relationship — it is the default position.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The alternative hypothesis (H₁) states there is a difference, an effect or a relationship.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is a hypothesis? | Q: What does the null hypothesis state? | Q: Write a suitable hypothesis for investigating whether Year 11 students spend more time on homework than Year 10 students.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A testable statement predicting the outcome of a statistical investigation. | That there is no difference, no effect or no relationship between the variables being studied. | Year 11 students spend more time on homework per week than Year 10 students.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always write your hypothesis before collecting any data — never change it to fit results. Use precise comparative language: 'greater than', 'less than', 'there is a relationship between'. Make sure your hypothesis mentions both variables clearly. In the exam, you may be asked to write or evaluate a hypothesis — check it is specific and testable. Know the difference between null and alternative hypotheses even if you do not use H₀/H₁ notation.
